mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT recover for two to four weeks, weekday trips generate more incidental shopping and dining visits, pushing RETAIL_REC above its prior four-week average over the next month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 28 days despite simultaneous week-over-week improvement in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT for at least two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp fall in RESIDENTIAL time signals more time spent outside home, and when that drop exceeds the recent range it raises retail visits within one to two weeks as people convert freed time into errands and discretionary purchases.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls at least 1.0 point below its prior weekly mean
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines over the next 14 days even after RESIDENTIAL drops below its prior weekly average by at least 1 point.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT drops abruptly while WORKPLACES does not, a commuting disruption or restriction shock suppresses discretionary stops and lowers RETAIL_REC over the following one to four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 5 points week-on-week while WORKPLACES is unchanged or higher
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days after a week with a >5 point TRANSIT drop and no matching WORKPLACES decline.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent PARKS strength during warm-weather weeks diverts time toward outdoor leisure and away from indoor shopping, so elevated PARKS mobility predicts lower RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days while PARKS stays above its recent weekly average throughout the period.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM rises together with RETAIL_REC, households are shifting from routine essential trips into broader shopping missions, and that co-movement should continue to lift retail mobility over the next one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM is above its prior week by at least 2 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to improve within 7 days after GROCERY_PHARM rises by 2 or more points from the prior week.

mechanism_narrative: A short-lived spike in PARKS followed by a drop in TRANSIT signals substitution toward outdoor local activity and away from city-center shopping trips, which should depress RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises while TRANSIT falls in the same week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall over the next 14 days after a week in which PARKS increases and TRANSIT decreases simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime, improving WORKPLACES mobility expands daytime exposure and lunch-hour shopping, so RETAIL_REC should be higher four weeks later even if grocery and park activity stay noisy.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its prior four-week average over the next 28 days despite a sustained rise in WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL stays elevated while TRANSIT stays depressed, people remain closer to home and make fewer discretionary retail trips, so RETAIL_REC will remain below its recent baseline over the next month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last 28-day mean even though RESIDENTIAL stays above baseline and TRANSIT stays below baseline for most of the next four weeks.
